items.title: An installed hook says which contract it was written against
items.description: Carry a version marker in every hook command dim installs, read it back to tell an out-of-date hook from a missing one, and have the installer replace a stale entry rather than append beside it.

items.title: A claim refuses when the gates are not installed
items.description: Have dim order claim refuse to issue an order while the session hooks are missing or stale, so a run cannot proceed behind gates that will record nothing.

items.title: A factory worktree refuses a commit with no running order
items.description: Refuse a commit made in a factory worktree while no order is running there, so work cannot land outside the record that is supposed to hold it.

items.title: post-commit writes the commit and its changed files
items.description: Record the commit and each file it touched with the added and removed counts git show --numstat reports, so the order's file rows stop depending on a skill typing them.

items.title: pre-commit writes the check row it already runs
items.description: Have the pre-commit gate record the command it ran and the code it exited with, since it already runs the repo's check and nothing writes that result.

items.title: An ended session stops the orders it held
items.description: Make --session required on claim and have SessionEnd stop every order that session holds, so an abandoned run leaves no order running forever.

items.title: Claiming an order moves its queue item
items.description: Have claim and stop write the queue item's transition in the same command, so the order record and the planner file cannot disagree about what is active.

items.title: Whatever writes the claim makes the worktree
items.description: Create the worktree and branch in the command that records them and remove the worktree when the order stops, so a claim can no longer name a path that never existed.

items.title: Score recall against LongMemEval
items.description: Port the LongMemEval dataset adapters so a published recall claim is measured against an external set rather than only the corpus-native one.

items.title: Tell two passages in one session apart
items.description: Give search a ref finer than a session so two graded passages from one session can be separated and bench can score the question instead of refusing it.

items.title: Draw labeled questions from handoff links
items.description: Grow the labeled set past one agent's sitting by drawing questions from handoff_link pairs, where a query and its known answer already exist.

items.title: Reciprocal-rank fusion
items.description: Fuse the cosine and keyword rankings, scored against the labeled set rather than argued.

items.title: Ledger of measured guidance cuts
items.description: Record append-only which guidance cuts a measurement confirmed or rejected, written when the runner decides a cut.

items.title: Whether raw turns belong in the index
items.description: Settle by benchmark whether indexing raw conversation turns helps retrieval, after they measured worse as input.

items.title: A self-maintaining loop in an app repo
items.description: Run dim-line-fix on a schedule against the faults a shipping repo's own crash reports name, with a memory of what was already attempted kept beside those reports.

items.title: Corrections as a source
items.description: Put rows in correction_label so a reworded repetition has a source that can catch it.

items.title: How a repository declares its isolation strategy
items.description: Name the requirements the workspace profile still leaves open beyond setup and teardown hooks: the isolation strategy, and containers, ports and disk.

items.title: What the factory wall cannot show
items.description: Give the board a threshold for how long is too long, a mark for the station-move event, a durable agent-to-name table, a project on every card and an operator record.

items.title: Fill the item view with the plan and the build
items.description: Carry the plan an order was given and the account of what it built into the item view, since what it holds today is only what the record already holds.

items.title: Queue selection and serialized integration
items.description: Take queue selection, serialized integration and queue-state enforcement into the order contract, and correct the skill that still types the commands wrong.

items.title: Read the item's own statement back
items.description: Have dim q order, dim q factory and the wall card show the --description recorded on claim, which is written but not yet read back.

items.title: Harness-neutral factory scheduler
items.description: Install the schedule in a host, claim the due queue work and record what each scheduled run executed.

items.title: The owner's verdict on a finished order
items.description: Record whether a finished order landed as it came, was sent back or was changed before landing, with the grounds whenever it was not the first.

items.title: Record the tier a role actually ran at
items.description: Add a field on the delegation event, joined against factory_order_finding, so whether a cheap checker raises fewer real findings than an expensive one can be asked.

items.title: Architecture review on a boundary
items.description: Run the read-only architecture dimension when the queue presents a change crossing a module, schema, queue or hook boundary.

items.title: PostToolUse as an installed event
items.description: Record tool activity from a PostToolUse hook that spools rather than writes, so a later pass reads it and a failing hook cannot break a session.

items.title: Run a formatter after an edit
items.description: Resolve the checkout from an edit event, run the repository's declared formatter against the changed paths, record the result and fail open.

items.title: The working-directory check
items.description: Compare the repo a git call is aimed at against the one the session belongs to, which only a hook on the tool call can do.

items.title: The weakening guard
items.description: Warn when a change weakens a test or a check, rather than blocking it.

items.title: Undoing an agent's writes
items.description: Record that an agent changed something and commit that record on a later pass, so a write can be undone.

items.title: The tooling chain in wake
items.description: Derive which CLIs a repo is actually worked with from the shell commands its sessions ran, once the threshold telling an interesting tool from a universal one is settled.

items.title: Split jsonc IO from its text edits
items.description: Settle whether the jsonc module grows a path-level edit or drops its IO, so every writer stops repeating the exists, read, append, check, back up, write sequence.

items.title: Two small jsonc edit infidelities
items.description: A comment trailing an array's last element labels the entry appended after it, and an edited CRLF file comes back with LF endings.

items.title: Each subcommand carries its own help
items.description: Print every dim subcommand's usage from a registry the way queries already do, so adding a command cannot leave the listing silently short.

items.title: q repeats classifies by meaning
items.description: Replace the stopword set, regex and character threshold that decide what a repeat is with meaning.

items.title: A schema edit announces itself
items.description: Derive the schema version from the schema text and the rebuild drop list from every table but an explicitly spared few, once the cost of that check on every command is known.

items.title: A stuck-slice counter
items.description: Count a slice's failed attempts across sessions, which a per-run bound inside the driver cannot see.

items.title: Whether checking pays
items.description: Join a finding's file against the later fix commits that came back to it, and checked slices against unchecked ones, once there are rows to join.

items.title: A judge for a refused finding
items.description: Make the third agent fire on a refusal that rests on whether a finding is true, and record how each went, rather than leaving the builder to reach for it.

items.title: Two label counts state different bases
items.description: Decide whether both the per-skill column and the scalars beside it join message, or whether rebuild reports the labels whose message did not come back.

items.title: q keywords ANDs every word
items.description: Rank by how many terms matched rather than requiring all of them, or say in the query's own output that it wants few words.

items.title: Whether the simplification pass pays
items.description: Run slices with and without the pass and score each arm by whether a later fix commit came back to what it touched.

items.title: The aimed simplification pass
items.description: Pick which untouched code has earned a simplification off q fixes, q rework and q exemplars rather than off whatever is open.

items.title: Why agents-md edits draw more fixes
items.description: Explain why files edited under agents-md draw four times more fixes afterward than before, the one station sample that did not clear.

items.title: The generated conventions block
items.description: Measure the guidance cuts already made by hand as characters removed against the calls they would have stayed resident for, before generating anything.

items.title: Gates for US spelling and banner comments
items.description: The two conventions a mechanism can hold; everything else there needs judgement and stays written.

items.title: The trimmed arm and rule inventory
items.description: The eval runner's first slice: an arm running a trimmed guidance surface, and an inventory of the rules it can cut.

items.title: A guidance-file arm for the runner
items.description: Deliver a trimmed guidance surface through a whole config directory written fresh inside the arm, with a test that reddens when a write goes through the symlink.

items.title: An index over code by meaning
items.description: Answer whether this shape was solved before where the shape is not in the filename, which needs a query that prints a file path as a ref so bench can grade it.

items.title: Extracting the toolchain that repeats
items.description: Delete the drifted script forks this repo already does once, and build the mise and env handling shared across the five checkouts.

items.title: Generating the machine-held conventions
items.description: Build the gates and earn one cut each; nothing generates a block until there are gates to hold the rules.

items.title: The routing tier
items.description: Score whether a prompt reaches the skill it should, revisited only if telemetry shows misroutes that editing descriptions did not close.

items.title: A markdown writer that replaces a heading
items.description: Replace a heading's byte range through an AST, which only the generated conventions block would call.

items.title: The scheduled sync is macOS-only
items.description: install-agent writes a launchd plist, so nothing schedules the sync on another platform.

items.title: Wire dim-factory to read queue.json
items.description: Teach the driver to read a planner file's own items through dim queue ready, so a queue.json is worked without retyping any item.

items.title: Brief the worker taking a ready item
items.description: Hand the builder the id, title and statement dim queue ready printed, unedited, so a claim never records a second version of an item.

items.title: Point the build order at the queue file
items.description: Give docs/build-order.md the argument, order and fence, and queue.json the state, so neither page restates what the other decides.

items.title: A claim refuses while the floor is stopped
items.description: Have dim order claim read factory_stop and refuse a new order while a stop is live, so stopping the floor stops work entering it rather than only recording that someone wanted it stopped.

items.title: The queue read and written as rows
items.description: Build dim queue add, ready and transition against the queue tables, ordering ready by priority then by when an item was added, and taking --blocks so a prerequisite found mid-slice becomes an edge.

items.title: The items moved out of the file
items.description: Import every item queue.json holds into the queue tables, carrying its id, title, statement and dependencies unchanged.

items.title: The planner file deleted
items.description: Delete queue.json, the half of src/queue-planner.ts that parses it, src/repo-queue.test.ts and every page that names it, in one slice.

items.title: Which project an order belongs to
items.description: Record the canonical owner/repo on every order and queue item and show it on the card, so one board can carry work from more than one repo.

items.title: A station that fills a queue
items.description: Write the station that turns a subject, a file or an issue tracker URL into queue items with their dependencies and priority.

items.title: The wall asks for the owner when it needs them
items.description: Send a notification when an order stops fenced or failed, since those are the states that need a person and they arrive when nobody is watching the board.

items.title: A test reading another test's commit
items.description: Isolate the factory order query test that picks up a commit sha another test wrote when the whole suite runs, since a check that fails for an unrelated reason is one people re-run rather than read.

items.title: The worktree a card names twice
items.description: Drop the stored worktree path from the order, since a path is true of one machine at one moment and the branch it is derived from is the durable identity.

items.title: Every moment says which agent it was
items.description: Write the actor on every order event rather than on three kinds of it, so an order's history names the planner, builder and reviewer that handled it.

items.title: An order's report read as columns rather than as one cell
items.description: Give each fact in dim q order its own column sized to what it holds, instead of packing the station, worktree, branch and reason into one cell joined by a pipe.

items.title: A way out of the item view you can see
items.description: Give the item dialog a close control, since Escape and a backdrop click both work and neither is visible on the surface they apply to.

items.title: Worktrees under a directory no tool owns
items.description: Move task worktrees from .claude/worktrees to .agents/worktrees, the harness-neutral convention this repo already follows for skills.

items.title: A moved checkout reads as a second repo
items.description: Key the repo tables on the owner/repo label the remote gives rather than on the git toplevel, so moving a checkout stops splitting one repo's rows into two.

items.title: What a tracker settled and what it did not
items.description: Write the page stating where this queue converges with an issue tracker and where it diverges, with the mechanism behind each divergence and no claim of a benchmark nobody ran.
